title: Gotrade Daily: Oil Climbs, Carnival and Jobs Data Tonight
summary: Oil climbs after Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz offer. Your US watchlist for tonight: CCL, KMX, NVDA, and XOM, plus JOLTS data at 10 a.m. ET.
body_markdown:
Tonight, **Carnival ([CCL](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/ccl/) )** is the most direct test. The cruise operator does not hedge its fuel, so oil prices flow straight into its earnings.


## Tonight's Watchlist


Stock Movement What to Watch


[CCL](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/ccl/) -0.49% Monday, reports before the open Consensus EPS of $1.42. Watch the full-year guidance as fuel costs rise.


[KMX](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/kmx/) -1.15% Monday, reports before the open Consensus EPS around $0.70. A read on used-car demand as loan rates climb.


[NVDA](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) +1.68% Monday A $150 billion buyback boost. Can that support hold as yields rise?


[XOM](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/xom/) +1.20% Monday The most direct read-through if oil keeps climbing.


## Tonight's Catalysts


### Carnival faces the fuel test


**Carnival ([CCL](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/ccl/) )** reports third-quarter results before the US open. According to[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/carnival-earnings-on-deck-can-summer-strength-offset-fuel-costs-93CH-4920583) , consensus sits at US$1,35 - US$1,36 in EPS on US$8,36 - US$8,40 billion in revenue. Carnival previously revised its full-year guidance for more than $500 million in added fuel costs. Demand is still strong, with 93% of 2026 capacity already booked, but CCL shares have fallen more than 20% in recent weeks.


### Job openings and consumer confidence


August JOLTS job openings data and the Conference Board consumer confidence index are due at[10:00 a.m. ET](https://www.financecalendar.com/us-consumer-confidence/) . The Fed already[raised rates](https://www.schwab.com/learn/story/fomc-meeting) in September.[CME FedWatch](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) data shows markets pricing roughly a 70% chance of another hike on October 28. That is market pricing, not a certainty. A stronger-than-expected print could push yields higher again.
